subject: API semver transition & SDK alignment for OrbitWorks integration
messages:
From: Anna Park <anna@orbitworks.co>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: OrbitWorks integration: API contract change request

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — OrbitWorks is excited about the latency and cost profile we saw. We have one ask from our engineering team: we need to coordinate a planned change to Redwood's /v1/predict API that will alter the response payload structure (removing the legacy 'tokens' array in favor of a new 'segments' object). This is a breaking change for our SDKs.

A few constraints from our side:
- We release SDKs on a monthly cadence and need at least a 60–90 day compatibility window to update and run CI across customer repos.
- We prefer semver-based versioning and need guidance about whether this change would be treated as a major bump (v2.0) versus a minor/compat shim.
- We also need a machine-readable compatibility matrix (CSV) so our CI can fail builds that rely on removed fields.

Could you share Redwood's deprecation policy/timeline and whether you can provide a backward-compatibility shim or dual-schema mode for the transition window? Happy to set up a sync.

Thanks,
Anna Park
Head of Integrations — OrbitWorks
anna@orbitworks.co

Attachment: orbitworks-internal-impact-notes.docx (referenced)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna@orbitworks.co>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 13:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: API semver transition & SDK alignment for OrbitWorks integration

Hi Anna — appreciate the clear ask. Looping in Laura (API roadmap) and Sergio (partner engineering) so we can get you a concrete plan.

High level: Redwood follows semver for public API surfaces. Breaking schema changes are treated as a major version (v2.0) and we aim to provide at least a 90-day deprecation window plus a compatibility header/mode where feasible. That said, there are two implementation options we can propose to OrbitWorks:

1) Dual-schema mode (recommended): run both payloads concurrently with a request header (X-Redwood-Legacy) for 90 days. Minimal perf impact and gives partners time to update.
2) Major version with adapter: publish v2.0 and offer an adapter library that maps 'segments' -> 'tokens' for two minor versions post-release. This avoids runtime branching but requires integrating the adapter.

Can Laura outline the technical constraints and draft a migration timeline? Sergio — can you confirm runtime/outages risk and whether the compatibility header is doable without large infra changes?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai

Anna — thanks for the details. I put together a short migration proposal after reviewing the API surface and our runtime concerns. See summary and attachments.

Summary (technical):
- Classification: breaking schema change -> Major version (v2.0).
- Compatibility approach: we can support a dual-schema mode behind X-Redwood-Legacy for 90 calendar days post v2.0 GA. During this window we will:
  * Accept both 'tokens' and 'segments' in responses and set X-Redwood-Legacy: true/false in responses to indicate which payload was used.
  * Emit deprecation warnings to logs and telemetry (no PII).
- Performance: negligible median latency change (~+3ms p50) under typical traffic, estimated +5–8% tail under pathological long-seq workloads.
- Rollout plan: staged canary -> region-wide -> global over 2 weeks.
- CI artifacts: we'll publish a redwood-compat-matrix.csv that lists which SDK releases are compatible with v1.x and v2.x.

Proposed timeline (dates are illustrative):
- 2027-04-05: Final API contract spec published and SDK compatibility matrix posted.
- 2027-04-19: v2.0 branch cut and internal QA sign-off.
- 2027-05-03: v2.0 staged rollout begins (canaries), dual-schema enabled by default.
- 2027-08-01: Dual-schema sunset; legacy 'tokens' removed entirely.

Attachments: orbitworks-migration-plan.pdf (detailed steps), redwood-compat-matrix.csv (placeholder), https://github.com/redwood-inference/orbitworks-integration/pull/84 (integration PR draft).

Notes: Sergio, we should include a small feature-flag gate per region for OrbitWorks' org id to let them opt-in early.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, API Platform
laura@redwood.ai

Attachment: orbitworks-migration-plan.pdf (11 pages)

Thanks Laura — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side:

1) CI integration: can you provide the redwood-compat-matrix.csv in machine-readable form (we prefer CSV with columns: sdk_name, sdk_version, api_compatibility, notes). We'll plug this into our nightly integration tests.
2) SDK pinning: For customers using OrbitWorks' Python SDK, can we rely on a simple pip requirement (>=1.5,<3.0) during the transition, or do you recommend pinning to a specific patch while we validate?
3) Can you share whether the feature-flag per-org opt-in will be available in the first canary window (the week of 2027-05-03)?

We've attached our internal migration checklist (orbitworks-ci-checklist.xlsx) to show where automated failures would be raised. If you can confirm the CSV and opt-in timing, we'll schedule an internal release to coincide with your staged rollout.

Appreciate the partnership — the dual-schema approach sounds like the least risky route for our customers.

Best,
Devon Chen
Lead Platform Engineer, OrbitWorks
